questions.question: Ava has \(4\) times as many stickers as Ben. Ava gives \(9\) of her stickers to Ben. Ava now has \(15\) more stickers than Ben. How many stickers did Ava start with?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) be Ben's starting stickers, so Ava starts with \(4x\). After Ava gives away 9, Ava has \(4x-9\) and Ben has \(x+9\). Ava now has 15 more than Ben:

\[(4x-9)-(x+9)=15\]
\[3x-18=15\]
\[3x=33\]
\[x=11\]

Ava started with \(4x=44\) stickers.

questions.question: Owen has twice as many trading cards as Maddie. Owen gives \(5\) of his cards to Maddie. Owen now has \(3\) more cards than Maddie. How many cards did Owen start with?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) be Maddie's starting cards, so Owen starts with \(2x\). After Owen gives away 5, Owen has \(2x-5\) and Maddie has \(x+5\). Owen now has 3 more than Maddie:

\[(2x-5)-(x+5)=3\]
\[x-10=3\]
\[x=13\]

Owen started with \(2x=26\) cards.

questions.question: Lena has five times as many buttons as Theo. Lena gives \(12\) of her buttons to Theo. Lena now has \(8\) more buttons than Theo. How many buttons did Lena start with?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) be Theo's starting buttons, so Lena starts with \(5x\). After Lena gives away 12, Lena has \(5x-12\) and Theo has \(x+12\). Lena now has 8 more than Theo:

\[(5x-12)-(x+12)=8\]
\[4x-24=8\]
\[4x=32\]
\[x=8\]

Lena started with \(5x=40\) buttons.

solution.exhibit_text:
In a parallelogram, consecutive angles are supplementary. Angles \(P\) and \(Q\) are consecutive:

\[6x+30=180\]

questions.question: Today, Ravi's age is \(\dfrac{1}{6}\) of Grace's age. In \(2\) years, Ravi's age will be \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of Grace's age. How old is Grace today?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(r\) be Ravi's age today and \(g\) be Grace's age today, so \(r=\dfrac{g}{6}\). In 2 years, \(r+2=\dfrac{g+2}{4}\). Substitute:

\[\dfrac{g}{6}+2=\dfrac{g+2}{4}\]
\[2g+24=3g+6\]
\[18=g\]

Grace is 18 today.

questions.question: Today, Priya's age is \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of her brother's age. In \(6\) years, Priya's age will be \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) of her brother's age. How old is her brother today?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(p\) be Priya's age today and \(b\) be her brother's age today, so \(p=\dfrac{b}{4}\). In 6 years, \(p+6=\dfrac{b+6}{2}\). Substitute:

\[\dfrac{b}{4}+6=\dfrac{b+6}{2}\]
\[b+24=2b+12\]
\[12=b\]

Her brother is 12 today.

questions.question: Today, Diego's age is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) of his sister's age. In \(5\) years, Diego's age will be \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) of his sister's age. How old is his sister today?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(d\) be Diego's age today and \(s\) be his sister's age today, so \(d=\dfrac{s}{3}\). In 5 years, \(d+5=\dfrac{s+5}{2}\). Substitute:

\[\dfrac{s}{3}+5=\dfrac{s+5}{2}\]
\[2s+30=3s+15\]
\[15=s\]

His sister is 15 today.

questions.question: There are \(7\) different puzzles on a shelf. Nora will choose \(2\) of these puzzles to bring to a friend's house. How many different pairs of \(2\) puzzles can she choose from the \(7\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
There are 7 ways to pick the first puzzle and 6 ways to pick the second, giving \(7\times6=42\) ordered picks. Since order doesn't matter for a pair, divide by 2:

\[42\div2=21\]

questions.question: Working at a constant rate, Emma can fold \(6\) shirts in \(15\) minutes. Working at his own constant rate, Noah can fold \(4\) shirts in \(8\) minutes. What is the total number of shirts the two of them can fold in one hour?

solution.exhibit_text: Emma folds \(6\) shirts every \(15\) minutes, which is \(\dfrac{6}{15}\times60=24\) shirts per hour. Noah folds \(4\) shirts every \(8\) minutes, which is \(\dfrac{4}{8}\times60=30\) shirts per hour. Together: \(24+30=54\) shirts in one hour.

questions.question: If \(7n\) is a positive even number, how many **odd** numbers are in the range from \(7n\) up to and including \(7n+9\)?

solution.exhibit_text: The range from \(7n\) to \(7n+9\), inclusive, contains 10 consecutive integers. Since \(7n\) is even, the integers alternate even, odd, even, odd, .... Out of 10 consecutive integers starting on an even number, exactly half — 5 — are odd.
